newsitem.title: THAILAND: Exiles protest at Burmese embassy in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Exiles protest at Burmese embassy in Bangkok.

text.p: About 15 Burmese exiles staged a protest on Monday outside the Burmese Embassy in Bangkok in support of recently suppressed anti-government student protests in Rangoon.

The exiles, representing eight anti-government organisations, demanded that Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) meet the students' demands for more political freedom and rights.
They also called on the SLORC to release all imprisoned students and political activists and enter into a dialogue with opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi and ethnic nationalities in the country.
Suu Kyi, who has denied any link with the student protestors, was asked to remain in her Rangoon residence by the SLORC after the student unrest.
A spokesman for the exiles said about 30 students had been rounded up by the military in Rangoon last weekend for alleged involvement in the street protests earlier this month.
"The SLORC cannot solve the problems of Burma by arresting and suppressing the people...they will only fuel the problems," said a statement issued by the group.
Meanwhile, the exiled All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF) said in a statement that three pro-democracy proponents were detained by the SLORC on Sunday.
It said the SLORC was applying pressure on teachers and civil servants whose children may have been involved in the street protests.
"It is easier for the military to curb the activities of these students by putting pressure on their parents," the ABSDF statement said.
Officials at the Burmese Embassy were not available for comment.
The exiles dispersed voluntarily after their protest.
About 2,000 university students participated in the protests in Rangoon early this month to demand greater political freedom and to speak out against poice brutality.
The government broke up the demonstrations and briefly detained more than 860 students.
The military have parked tanks at Rangoon city hall, closed universities, blocked a few roads in the capital and prevented students from regrouping.
